reviews.reason: The primary CIF parses without warnings and symmetry-expands in Im-3 (No. 204) to a fully occupied, ordered 34-atom conventional cell Ca2Fe8Sb24 (Z=2), with a=b=c=9.17797 angstrom and V=773.10753 angstrom^3; primitive standardization gives one 17-atom CaFe4Sb12 formula unit, so the reported Z is not a distinct realization. All 27 observed maxima above 5 sigma are covered by calculated reflections within 0.0122 degrees 2theta, no body-centering-forbidden odd-N position exceeds 3.3 sigma, and no separate important unexplained reflection survives. An independent whole-profile refit with the submitted coordinates fixed gives unit-weight Rwp=4.60% and RMS=0.129 versus baseline noise 0.102, close to a Pawley-like independent-intensity bound of Rwp=4.40% and RMS=0.124. The trace also shows several pseudo-Voigt, Voigt, split-profile, and direct-integration intensity extractions converging on Sb coordinates near the submitted (0, 0.33495, 0.16169), so support is atomic-coordinate based rather than prototype naming or peak positions alone. Orbit multiplicities 2a/8c/24g uniquely enforce Ca/Fe/Sb ordering at full occupancy in this symmetry. Periodic shells are chemically coherent (Fe-Sb 2.555 angstrom, sixfold Fe; Sb-Sb 2.968/3.030 angstrom; Ca-Sb 3.414 angstrom, twelvefold Ca) with no overlaps; a purely ionic automated bond-valence assignment is unavailable for this intermetallic framework but there is no demonstrable charge or bond-valence impossibility. No concrete diffraction-compatible ordering, symmetry-lowered superstructure, or distinct framework remains supported, so another attempt is unlikely to add a materially different viable candidate.
